activity_context.topic_title: The Parametric Equations of a Line

feedback.problem:
Fill in the missing parts in the parametric equations below that describe all the points on the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ},$ where $P(4,1,-1)$ and $Q(6,5,1).$

| $x=$ | $4+2t$ | $t\in [0,$ {{field-1}} $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y=$ | $1+4t$ |  |
| $z=$ | {{field-2}} |  |
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the line passing through the given points. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2t \\ 4t \\ 2t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4+2t \\ 1+4t \\ -1+2t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

To get the equations for the line segment, we take only $t\in [0,1].$ Notice that substitution of $t=0$ in the above equation gives the coordinates of $P$ and substitution of $t=1$ gives the coordinates of $Q.$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ}$ are the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=4+2t \\ y=1+4t \\ z=-1+2t\end{aligned}\,\,t\in [0,1]
$$
